label: early a/p/y/k/1 input in a background-token prefix (original phase)
explanation: Original-phase input feature (98% of mass in phase 0, almost silent in copy phase). Fires mainly on inputs a and p (55% of mass), then y, k, 1 (rates 15-33% vs 5% base). Strongest when the token arrives after a prefix made of tokens n/x/u/g/h/i/o/2/v/q (top examples: x u g u [a], x n u g [p]); a prior occurrence of a, p, y, k, 1 or other tokens outside that group suppresses it, so a later repeat of the set usually stays silent. Activations are largest at t=0 and t=3. Weak residual firing on other first-occurrence letters (f, j, b, r, m) and on <DEL> right after such a token, which the predicate misses (~27% of mass). Does not fire on copy-phase outputs. Simple token predicate (phase 0 and in_tok in {a,p,y,k,1}) gets mass recall 0.79 but precision 0.43; adding the prefix condition gives F1 about 0.64 on dev.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=0: k, y, 1, p; t=1: a, p, y, k; t=2: a, p, y, k) and the first original token (most: n, x, u, g, i, h; least: t, y, m, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, t=4, t=3.
